2010.kid: A mast with three flat antennas, each covering a slice of the area around it. It talks to all the phones nearby by radio and sends their parcels on to its controller.
2010.nerd: A 3G base station (NodeB): three sector antennas, the HSDPA scheduler and HARQ (MAC-hs), and an Iub line back to its RNC, often E1 lines with ATM or a microwave link in 2010.

up.kid: The tower takes your parcel off the radio and sends it down the line to the controller, still in its radio envelope.
up.nerd: The NodeB ends the air interface (WCDMA, HARQ) and forwards the RLC pieces over Iub to the RNC; it doesn’t open them.

down.kid: The tower queues your parcel and sends it to your phone by radio when it’s your phone’s turn.
down.nerd: MAC-hs queues the RNC’s pieces per phone, and the scheduler sends them in the 2 ms slots and codes it picks.
